question: NSAIDs for Discogenic lower back pain, does it help?
search_summary: Europe PMC: 3 searches, 40 new records screened, 2 suggested. Answer uses checked cards only. AI-checked, not clinician-reviewed.

pico.p: Adults with discogenic lumbar low back pain

suggestions.title: Multidisciplinary expert consensus on clinical diagnosis and therapies for low back pain.
suggestions.citation: Gao B, Chai R, Wang G, Song Y, Shang L, Huang J, Cao X, Hai Y, Luo Z, Chinese Society for the Study of the Lumbar Spine, Chinese Association of Spine. Multidisciplinary expert consensus on clinical diagnosis and therapies for low back pain. Bone research 2026.
suggestions.why: Current multidisciplinary consensus summarizes diagnostic pathway and conservative treatment options, including NSAIDs, for low back pain.

suggestions.title: Low back pain (chronic).
suggestions.citation: Chou R. Low back pain (chronic). BMJ clinical evidence 2010.
suggestions.why: Broad chronic low back pain review summarizes oral drug treatments, helping frame NSAID evidence when discogenic data are sparse.

gaps: No placebo-controlled trial was found for NSAIDs in discogenic low back pain specifically.
Evidence comes mostly from mixed low back pain or observational studies, so certainty is low.
Short follow-up dominates; long-term pain relief and function from NSAIDs remain unclear.
Applicability to patients without Modic changes or with acute flares is uncertain.

answer.answer: NSAIDs may help some discogenic low back pain patients short term, but current cards do not show clear NSAID-specific benefit; the key caveat is that evidence is either uncontrolled stepped care or a short-term trial without effect sizes or CIs.
actions: Do not present NSAIDs as proven discogenic-specific treatment.
If used, frame benefit as possible short-term symptom relief only.
Do not rely on the stepped-care cohort to justify NSAIDs alone.
Prefer shared decision-making: evidence is uncertain and comparative advantages are unclear.
Do not change practice solely because all groups improved in the ketoprofen trial.
Reassess early and progress care if response is inadequate.

comparison.title: Mechanical methods vs NSAIDs for discogenic low back pain
comparison.finding: All groups improved; MIT was best on VAS and Schober, McKenzie best on Laitinen; ketoprofen not clearly best.

comparison.title: Stepped care for Modic discogenic low back pain: 53.6% met the …
comparison.design: observational cohort using routine care data
comparison.finding: 53.6% responded at 12 months after stepped care starting with celecoxib, but no control group.

agreement: Both cards suggest improvement can occur in discogenic low back pain care pathways.
Both cards do not establish a clear NSAID-specific treatment effect.
Both are limited for choosing NSAIDs confidently in practice.
conflicts: The trial suggests mechanical treatments may outperform ketoprofen on some outcomes.
The cohort cannot separate celecoxib effects from later injections, antibiotics, natural history, or expectancy.
Trial evidence is short term; cohort follow-up is 12 months but uncontrolled.
